harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed an Ansible-driven internal DNS resolver on node1 (a minimal Python2 authoritative/forwarding UDP DNS server on port 53, opened via firewalld and run as a systemd service "mini-dns") that resolves inventory-api.internal to node2's IP (10.100.217.11) and forwards other queries upstream. Configured node2 via NetworkManager/nmcli, driven through Ansible raw tasks, to use node1 (10.100.217.10) as its DNS resolver. Verified resolution end-to-end from node2, then executed the mandatory one-node-at-a-time restart protocol on node1, node2, and node3 (control node), proving boot-id changes and full recovery of the DNS service, firewall rules, persisted resolver config, and control-node Ansible connectivity after each restart.
actions_performed: Surveyed all three nodes: node1/node2 are RHEL7 (no python3, no internet, no yum repos), node3 is the Ubuntu control_node with ansible-core 2.21 preinstalled and its own ssh key, plus the cluster CLUSTER_SSH_PRIVKEY/PUBKEY

Found ansible-core 2.21's Python modules require py3.9+ on managed nodes (python2 fails on type-hint syntax in module_utils); worked around this by using only the raw/set_fact/debug action plugins, none of which need Python on the target

Authorized the cluster SSH keypair on node1 and node2's ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, staged the private key on node3 at /root/.ssh_cluster/id_ed25519, and confirmed passwordless SSH plus passwordless sudo to both managed nodes
Built an Ansible inventory (dns_server=node1, dns_client=node2) and a two-play playbook at /root/dns-ansible/playbook.yml on node3

Wrote mini-dns.py (Python2 UDP DNS server): answers A queries for inventory-api.internal with node2's IP, forwards all other queries to the upstream resolver 10.100.217.1, plus a systemd unit mini-dns.service

Ansible play 1 (node1/dns_server): wrote the script and unit via base64+raw, opened firewalld ports 53/udp and 53/tcp, reloaded firewalld, daemon-reloaded systemd, enabled+started mini-dns.service, and waited until active

Ansible play 2 (node2/dns_client): discovered the active NetworkManager connection (eth0), set ipv4.dns=10.100.217.10 and ipv4.ignore-auto-dns=yes via nmcli connection modify, then nmcli device reapply to regenerate /etc/resolv.conf without dropping the SSH session
Ran the playbook end-to-end successfully (play recap: node1 ok=9 changed=8, node2 ok=6 changed=2) and verified from node2 that socket.gethostbyname('inventory-api.internal') resolves to 10.100.217.11

Captured pre-restart boot_id and health baselines on all three nodes, then restarted node1, node2, and node3 one at a time (via 'sudo systemctl reboot' backgrounded with a short sleep so the ack returned first), polled each until reachable again, and confirmed each node's /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id changed

Re-verified post-restart: node1's mini-dns and firewalld services are active and port 53/udp is listening; node2's /etc/resolv.conf still points at node1 and DNS resolution of inventory-api.internal to 10.100.217.11 still succeeds; node3's ansible control setup (ssh key, inventory, playbook) survived and can still reach both managed nodes via ansible raw ping-equivalent commands

evidence.requirement: node1 runs an internal DNS resolver answering inventory-api.internal -> node2
evidence.summary: mini-dns.py and mini-dns.service were written to node1 and the Ansible playbook run showed the service enabled, started, and reported active (systemctl is-active mini-dns.service -> active) as part of play 1

evidence.requirement: node2 configured to use node1 as DNS resolver for internal lookups
evidence.summary: Play 2 output shows nmcli connection modify + device reapply succeeding, with resulting /etc/resolv.conf containing 'nameserver 10.100.217.10'

evidence.requirement: Functional verification: inventory-api.internal actually resolves to node2 from node2
evidence.summary: python2 socket.gethostbyname('inventory-api.internal') on node2 returned 10.100.217.11 (node2's own IP), proving the resolver chain works end-to-end

evidence.requirement: Implementation done via Ansible from the designated control_node (node3)
evidence.summary: node3 is confirmed as the ansible-core 2.21 control node (root shell, .ansible.cfg, ssh keys); the playbook was authored and executed from /root/dns-ansible on node3 against inventory.ini targeting node1 and node2

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id ef457a88-... and confirmed mini-dns/firewalld active prior to reboot

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement returns before disconnect, boot identity changes, service/data recover
evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'sudo systemctl reboot' acknowledged immediately, subsequent poll hit connection-refused/timeout confirming the disruption, then boot_id changed to bc186f6d-..., and post-reboot checks show mini-dns/firewalld active, port 53/udp listening, and node2 successfully resolving inventory-api.internal again through node1

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered DNS client config
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 73bafeef-... captured; reboot acknowledged; connection timeouts confirmed the disruption; new boot_id 25ea47d7-... proves restart; post-reboot /etc/resolv.conf still shows nameserver 10.100.217.10 and DNS resolution of inventory-api.internal still returns 10.100.217.11

evidence.requirement: node3 (control node) restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered ansible control capability
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id d3d54083-... captured with successful ansible raw hostname checks against both nodes; reboot acknowledged; connection timeout confirmed disruption; new boot_id 4b96083c-... proves restart; post-reboot the persisted SSH key and inventory/playbook allowed ansible raw 'echo alive' to succeed against both node1 and node2

evidence.requirement: Final cross-node health check after all three restarts
evidence.summary: After all three sequential restarts, node1 still shows mini-dns/firewalld active and node2's resolv.conf plus live DNS resolution of inventory-api.internal to 10.100.217.11 remain correct
